transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… what brings me in is I’m just really tired. Like, exhausted in a way that sleeping doesn’t seem to fix. I keep thinking maybe it’s just work, because being a manager is always a lot—meetings, emails, people needing things, and then I get home and there’s still dinner and normal life stuff. But lately even a regular workday and just getting through dinner at home feels heavier than it should.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like, such as hobbies or spending time with friends and family, as much as you did before feeling this exhaustion?

Yeah… not as much. I mean, I usually really love painting—like I’ll get all my brushes out and lose a whole afternoon without even noticing. And I like going to museum exhibits too, just kind of wandering and looking at things, even the little description plaques, which my family makes fun of me for reading every word.

But lately my paints are just sitting there. I see them and think, “I should,” and then I just… don’t. And there was an exhibit I would normally be excited about, but I couldn’t make myself care enough to go. It feels weird, because those are very “me” things.
Have you been feeling sad most of the time since you started noticing this exhaustion?

Yeah… I think so. Most days lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, gray feeling, like I’m already disappointed in the day before it’s even started. It’s not always dramatic crying or anything—sometimes I still get up and do what I’m supposed to do—but it’s just there.

It’s funny, I used to be more of a morning person, or at least I’d make coffee and look at the light in the kitchen and think about what needed doing. Now I’ll stand there and notice the dishes or some random thing on the counter and it all just feels… flat. Like the whole day is already weighted down.
How long have you been feeling this way?

About a month, I think. It’s a little hard to pin down because at first I was just sort of unusually energized and really driven—like I was pushing through things and taking on more—and then it shifted into this low, heavy feeling that’s been sticking around. But the whole swing, from that revved-up phase to now feeling persistently down, has been around a month.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Not really… I keep trying to think of one, but the things I usually look forward to just don’t land the same. Painting is the big one—I normally love setting everything out, mixing colors, making a mess of the table. Lately the supplies are just sitting there, and I keep walking past them like, “Maybe later,” and then later never happens.

And museums, too. There was this exhibit I probably would’ve dragged someone to before—or gone by myself, honestly, because I like taking my time. But I just couldn’t make myself care enough to go. It’s strange, because those are usually the things that make me feel like myself.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in almost all activities you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, “almost all” sounds so big, but… the things I usually really love, like painting, I just don’t touch now. The brushes and paints are sitting there, and I keep meaning to start, but I don’t.

And museums—I used to love just wandering around an exhibit, even by myself. Lately I can’t make myself care enough to go, which is odd because normally that’s the kind of thing I’d plan my whole afternoon around.
Have you experienced any periods of elevated mood or increased energy during the past month?

Yeah… earlier in the month there was definitely a stretch where I felt really charged, like unusually upbeat and convinced my ideas were brilliant. I remember making all these plans—some of them were probably fine, but I was very sure about them.

And then if my husband asked even a normal question, like “Are you sure that’s a good idea?” I’d get irritated really fast. Which is funny because he questions everything, even what brand of paper towels to buy, but this felt different… like I went from feeling great to snapping at him over nothing.
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide since you started feeling this way?

I… I’m not sure how to answer that. I mean, I don’t think I’ve been sitting around planning anything, if that’s what you mean. Sometimes my mind goes to weird places when I’m tired, but then I’ll get distracted by something stupid, like whether I remembered to move the laundry, and then I’m annoyed because the laundry smells damp.

So… I guess I haven’t really noticed anything clear like that.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?

A little, I think. I haven’t been weighing myself every day or anything, but I’ve been sort of picking at meals… or I’ll get busy at work and realize I just never ate lunch. Which is ridiculous because there’s a salad place right downstairs, and I keep buying those little containers of soup thinking I’ll be organized.

But yeah, my skirts are fitting a bit looser lately. I’m not trying to lose weight, it’s just… food hasn’t been something I’m really paying attention to.
Do you feel like your low mood is interfering with your ability to function at work or at home?

Yeah, I mean… not completely. I’m still going to work, still getting the basic stuff done at home. It’s not like everything has fallen apart.

But I am slower making decisions at work, which is awkward because, you know, I’m supposed to be the person people come to for decisions. And at home I’ve been less dependable with plans—like I’ll say we should do something as a family and then I kind of fade out of it or forget to follow through.

And I haven’t really been doing my art things much lately, which is… that’s usually how I stay connected with people. I keep meaning to go, and then I just don’t.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or feeling like it's harder to get things done physically since you started feeling this way?

Kind of, yes. Not like I’m physically dragging my feet around the house exactly, but at work people have noticed I’m… slower, I guess.

In meetings, someone will ask me something, and there’s this pause before I can get the thought together and actually say it. One of my staff sort of joked about it—well, not joked meanly, just noticed—and then I started noticing it too. Like my words are stuck in traffic.

It’s embarrassing, because meetings already have enough weird pauses, and then everyone starts looking at their notebooks or pretending to check the agenda. But yes, I think I am slower to respond than usual.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly physically, not just thinking more slowly?

I’m not sure it’s my body exactly. I don’t feel like I’m shuffling around or anything dramatic like that. It’s more… in meetings, when someone asks me a question, there’s this lag before I answer.

My staff has noticed it too, which is the part that makes me self-conscious. Like there’s a pause before I can get my thoughts and the words moving. Physically I guess my mouth is slower, if that makes sense, but I don’t know if I’m moving slower walking around.
Do you feel like your body is moving more slowly than usual?

Not so much my whole body, I don’t think. I’m not, like, walking in slow motion or anything.

It’s more that in meetings, if someone asks me something, there’s this pause before I answer. My staff has noticed it too, which is… not great when you’re supposed to be the manager. It’s like I can’t get my thoughts and words lined up fast enough.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Restless or fidgety? Not really in the sense of tapping my foot or pacing around the room. I mean, I do adjust my papers a lot in meetings, but that’s probably just because meetings are awkward and everyone has too many agendas and not enough coffee.

What I’ve noticed more is the opposite, kind of. My staff has noticed I’m slower to answer questions in meetings—like someone asks me something and there’s this pause before I can get my thoughts and words moving. It’s… uncomfortable, because I can feel everyone waiting.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

I mean… not really like I used to. I usually love painting—like, I have all my brushes and little jars set up—and I can spend forever wandering around museum exhibits. Or I used to.

Lately the paint stuff just sits there untouched. I’ll look at it and think I should do something, but then I just… don’t care enough to start. And I keep meaning to go to the museum, because there’s an exhibit I would normally be excited about, but I can’t seem to make myself go. It feels weird, because those are usually my things.
Would you say your low mood is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

I’d probably say mild most of the time… though it doesn’t feel like nothing, if that makes sense.

Most days lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts. It’s not like I’m completely unable to function, but it’s there in the background. Mornings are the worst for it, I think—well, mornings have never been my favorite, but this is different. It’s just kind of a gray start to everything.
Would you describe your low mood as being consistently mild or are there times when it feels more moderate to severe?

I think it stays more on the mild side, honestly. It’s not usually this dramatic thing where I can’t get out of bed or anything like that.

It’s more like… most mornings lately I wake up and there’s this heavy, gray feeling already there, like I’m disappointed in the day before anything’s even happened. Which sounds a little ridiculous when I say it out loud—like the day hasn’t even had a chance to be annoying yet, you know? But that’s how it feels. Not severe, just… there, most days.
Would you say there are any days when your low mood feels worse than mild?

Maybe a little, but I’d still call it mild overall. It’s more that most days lately I wake up with that heavy, gray feeling, like I’m already disappointed in the day before it’s even started.

And then sometimes, if I’ve got a full workday ahead or even just errands—honestly, errands can feel more annoying than work sometimes—it kind of colors everything. But I don’t think it usually tips into something really severe. It’s just… there, heavier some mornings than others.
Are there any days when you feel like your low mood is more than just mild?

I mean… maybe a little more some days, but I’d still put it in the mild category most of the time.

It’s more that lately, a lot of mornings I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling already there, like I’m disappointed in the day before it’s even started. Which is strange, because nothing has happened yet—unless you count my alarm, which honestly is offensive enough on its own. But no, I don’t think it usually becomes really severe. It’s just… heavier some mornings.
Are there any days when your low mood feels more than just mild?

Yeah… I mean, some mornings it feels a little heavier, but I still don’t know that I’d call it more than mild. It’s more that lately I wake up most days with this heavy, gray feeling already sitting there, like I’m disappointed in the day before it even starts.

And then I’ll be making coffee or staring at my closet trying to decide what to wear, which somehow becomes this whole unnecessary ordeal, and I’m like, why am I already tired of today? But it’s not usually… I don’t know, extreme. Just there.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the severity of the patient's low mood, which directly corresponds to depressed mood.

patient.answer:
I mean… maybe a little more some days, but I’d still put it in the mild category most of the time.

It’s more that lately, a lot of mornings I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling already there, like I’m disappointed in the day before it’s even started. Which is strange, because nothing has happened yet—unless you count my alarm, which honestly is offensive enough on its own. But no, I don’t think it usually becomes really severe. It’s just… heavier some mornings.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's low mood is consistently mild or if there are fluctuations
doctor.question: Are there any days when your low mood feels more than just mild?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about the severity of the patient’s low mood, which directly corresponds to depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, some mornings it feels a little heavier, but I still don’t know that I’d call it more than mild. It’s more that lately I wake up most days with this heavy, gray feeling already sitting there, like I’m disappointed in the day before it even starts.

And then I’ll be making coffee or staring at my closet trying to decide what to wear, which somehow becomes this whole unnecessary ordeal, and I’m like, why am I already tired of today? But it’s not usually… I don’t know, extreme. Just there.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent low mood, loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities, changes in weight, and psychomotor retardation, which have been present for about a month, meet the diagnostic criteria for a mild depressive episode.
